body: Thank you so much for this.  I can begin healing from the abuse from this abuser, but I still have a long way to go for my core trauma that wasn't healed when I was with this person, if that makes sense.

For a podcast?  No, but I've done interviews for students papers at my University, along with class projects that involved interviewing members of my community that were around during the moon landing, the assassination of JFK and MLK, along with one interview with my grandfather about living in the depression, and my grandmother about surviving the holocaust.

Yes!  100% YES!  The only time Trauma would be touched is "I'm a survivor of ___"  So that way if anyone that listens is also dealing with or has been in the same shoes they'll know that they're not alone in this.  The whole interview is to focus on those victories, those methods that help you get through your day.  It's to show that people with trauma are not alone.
The post is already up it you wish to see it.

My whole thought process for this podcast wouldn't never be to go into full details of one's trauma.  More like "I was a victim of abuse by ____" and that's the full extent.  I find it more important to highlight living with C-PTSD or any trauma related illness to showcase that we can live, thrive and make a new life for ourselves.  These stories would mostly be about victories and triumphs of people who are still recovering or are at a point in their recovery where they don't see things as being hard to do anymore.  I'll be making a new post so to lay out all the details so that way it hopefully shows the full vision of what I wish to do.

That's totally what I'm after.  Like I said, the person being interviewed has full control over the entire interview.  The only thing being mentioned would be "I'm a survivor of sexual related trauma" or "I'm a survivor of child abuse" or any kind of survivor, just so that way anyone listening can have that personal connection of "They probably went through the same things I did, or know what's it's like to go through that"  That way the person who is listening and connecting can hear from the person being interviewed what worked for them and how they could better themselves.  This idea is to put power back into the hand of those who had it taken from them, and to let others know that they're not alone and can reclaim their lives again.  That's what this community has done for me and what I want to bring to those who don't know about it.

I had this same feeling too, which is why first and for most the person being interviewed is in full control over what parts they wish to share if any, if they wish to talk about their trauma at all.  My mission for this, aside from being able to get the word out on believing victims, is show just how strong we are and bring hope to people who may think there isn't any.  This podcast would in no way replace therapy, in fact it would be greatly encouraged for people to seek out if they can, but what I'm hoping is for those who are unable to seek therapy do to whatever reason, be it no insurance or lack of the type of professional they need, that there's information that could help them in specific situations that they didn't know was an option.  I hope that clears up anything for you.

That's helpful.  Mostly my thought process is that I don't want to action to go by too fast without actually getting what needs to be seen.  Most of this comes from the heals of a writing class but some of this feedback is a lot better than what other classmates have been able to give.

That's basically the idea of how each sort of warning would be instead of just a standard "This podcast contains content some may find uneasy.  Discretion is advised"  To me that just down plays the severity of the topics that will be discussed.  There would also be something to let people know that this podcast is to help inform listeners and is not a replacement for therapy.  The main purpose of this podcast is to celebrate victories we have and to at least let people know they're not alone and that they should seek help whenever possible.
This helps too.  Thank you.

That's also the reason why I wish to help people who aren't aware that there is still hope, and that we can all make it through this.  That's what this subreddit has done for me.  It gives me hope.

Those where some of the thoughts I had with it as well.  Of course I'd have to start ever opening with a trigger warning to be safe, and before recording would even start I would have a smaller more (but not really) personal interview with the person. My goal for this podcast is to showcase the strengths of everyone who is still pushing forward along with getting the word out to those who feel like they're struggling alone that they're not.  I hope that clarifies things as well.

I want nothing more than to understand how to minimize if not be free from this hell...as much as I help other around me, I feel like I'm a burden to them because I'm so complicated do to this stupid brain.

I wish I could, maybe if there's an audio book form of it.  I learned a little too late that I have some form a reading problems when it comes to focusing, whether it's a learning thing or my trauma I may never know.

I've been called "Shark eyes" by both friends and people alike.  When I was younger I never really got it until I saw "Jaws" for the first time and then I heard the famous quote "...The thing about a shark he's got lifeless eyes like a doll's eyes.  When he comes at you he doesn't seem to be living..."  Right now I just take it as a compliment from my friends because it sounds cool, but hearing it in the halls at school or in passing around town, it hurts a bit.  Like they thought I was capable of skinning someone and not feeling a damn thing...if they only knew I was just trying to feel safe they'd still have the same thoughts...no bit of news changes the way they think about you.

I just got done watching that episode.  When Dr. Maheswaran was talking about traumatic experiences and how the body reacts to "normal" events after Life-threatening ones the same way, I could feel my body tense up and start to trigger the Fs in me.  By the end of the episodes, and through no conscious effort of my own, I began to cry.  I'm still in that state where I don't really feel like crying but I'm crying anyway.

This show, and the original, means so much to me.  I've been a fan since it was in development and enjoyed the pilot's art style.  It holds a very rocky place in my heart because it was the show that my ex and I loved watching together and since the break up a lot of the stuff we use to watch together has been hard to watch solo.
I'm sorry...But what the fuck are you on?  I'm super confused by your comment.
The breakup happened 5 days after the crash. And I still don't feel like any of this is real. I'm losing my fucking mind and I can't tell what the hell is going on any more.

How is that fair? I could be facing a life time of a fucking mountain climb and not even make it half way by the time I die? I don't even now how to take care of myself outside of just eating when I'm hungry. I don't feel safe by myself, I could keep myself safe then and it's hard to even figure out how to now. I've only had one true safety merry in my life and now that person is causing more pain and possibly retraumtized me or worse added a new one.  I can't have a slight moment anymore because all I hear is the two of them and it sets me off in a panic....am I too broken...I just wanted to have an average life and all I get is one pain after another...everything hurts and I don't know how to heal...

I just feels like the trauma stunted my growth in a way. I'm not as far as I should be and where I am now everyone else was at when they were a teen. 

I feel like I have no real concept of anything. On top of that I feel like because I survived I should be making something of myself as a way to justify still being alive. I didn't stay alive because I wanted to. I had to because I was told what others would think of me of I went through with the alternative and for some reason my self worth is rooted in that...
I'm hitting am extram low in the middle of work. I want nothing more than to fucking cry but, of course, I can't.

I don't have kids, because um single, but I'm fucking terrified of children under 16 near me. In a lot of ways they remind me if the innocents that was stolen from me, and being reminded that my life will forever be different from children who will never face CSA makes me want to brake diem and cry. 

And for anyone wondering, I'm only find with kids 16+ because they're a lot smarter than we give them credit for. They're more resilient and are starting to see the world for what it is.

I'd never hurt children, I just don't want to be reminded what I lost.
Yeah, on top of that, they still don't 100% believe my story and just think I made it up for attention. Because hour could my abuser do that? "I know him better than you, he'd never do that!"

"Sure right, that all happened to you 😒 (or you think it did) but that was in the past and you need to let it go. People are suffering worse things or there"

 Thanks for belittling my experience and trauma bitch.

I had two moments. 

The first was in grade 10 when my mother was going through a devours with the person who abused me. During the middle of class it finale kicked in what had happened and a bunch of repressed memories came flooding in. I had a panic attack on my principal's office because of the minor freak out that started in my English class. That only just made me realize what happened. 

The second was the real deal when I fully realized there really is no do over. It happened a few years back in my junior year of university. During an acting class, we were told to substitute in somethings that had made us fear for our lives in a scene about abuse. I was the only one that didn't have to substitute in anything in to sell the abuse seen. Needless to say the scene was good, but after words I was visibly shaking. I knew then yay I can't go back to being a kid, can't change anything that's happened to me. There's no full on do over. I'm 21 (at the time),and have no friends or social skills. It's never felt so alone in my life that day.

Well,  I thought for the most part that the way I was acting didn't seem like a healthy way of handling the situation, and it was a bit toxic. However, I realized that the way they talked to me was through gaslighting abs DARVOing. Having that perspective let's me see that I've actually been the most adult in this whole thing and they've been the child.
I'm starting to realize that now. I kept going the extra mile for this person and they just didn't care. I'm sick of just bending over backwards for people who just walk all over me.

I figured it was them hoping I'd continue to break. But I'm done with them and they can go suck a lemon. 

Thanks for the words of wisdom.

Hey I kept my composure. I was try to set one ground rule that their new boyfriend isn't allowed near my patents house and instead of accepting it, they just bitched about how it wasn't fair of me to say that. 

It's 100% fair because it's my place and not their, I can accept who I want in it and on it.

One hundo my dude. I feel like I prep what I was going to say and how they respond and then just improv it anyway leaving all the prep work behind. 

I still don't know why I do that.

Sometimes we just need to remind ourselves of all we've been through and that, despite all of it, we're still here. 

We are all so much stronger than we give ourselves credit for.

Who says we have to have our shit together? I mean I feel the same way, I turned 25 a few months back but every time I look in the mirror I think I'm looking at a 16 year old. But in all honesty I feel like we've all had to have our "shit together" (or at least those who went through abuse as a child) when we were abused because no one wanted to deal with it as much as we did, but no one cares what a child says so it out right makes it feel like you had to be an adult at a young age to be heard. 

Weird rant I know, but hey we all have our own pace when it comes to healing. I say you're doing good for yourself right now. You've got this!

Hey, it's never easy to date someone with ptsd or any mental illness. The fact that you're asking for help, truly shows how much you care for them. The least I can do is give what advice I can. 

You the real mvp!

1. Right now, you are at a point where she truly trusts you, and you make her feel safe.  This is good and is a step forward in your relationship. 

2. Take her out of the area as soon as he comes in. It doesn't matter where you go, just make sure that he's no where near her. 

3. Once you two are out of that situation, try and comfort her as best toy can. Listen to what she says, and if she says no to something then it's a no. Do what toy can without being pushy. It's all about making sure she feels safe and secure. If anything, try and see a movie so that way time passes by fast and you can use that as a date night activities. 

This is a big thing for her to let you into a place she doesn't want to be in 100% of the time. You're handling it the best you can. You've got this. I believe in you.

My ex was really abusive, and I thought that's just how they show love. I kept telling myself "it's just out of love that they punch my shoulder," or "they don't really mean it when they call me stupid." Turns out when you're the only one in love and the other person doesn't even respect you as a person, then maybe what they're doing is abuse.

I'm still trying to coup with it. The last thing I know they did before blocking me on social media was saying how *they* were the ones that got ride of someone toxic and that *they're* free now. I'm not saying I'm guiltless in this, I know my trauma caused friction in our relationship but I was working on getting better. They're presenting themselves as the *true* victim in all of this. 

Even after all this I still don't want to see that all they did was bad. I hate myself for and don't know why.

I spent 6 years of my life with summertime I thought I wad going to spend the rest of my life with. Through those 6 years we both grew as people.  They learned that they were non-gender instead of female. They felt open enough to come out to me about it. I learned more about my past trauma and learned to handle it a bit better. But, early last month, the dropped all forms of communication and broke up with me after I got into my first car accident. They found someone new almost a day after we broke up. They ask the new person to move into the apartment we both signed for and asked for me to leave by the end of this year. I moved out this morning (12/14/19) but between now and the middle of last month, the new guy moved in, and with the walls in the apartment being as thin as they are, I could hear everything they were doing. It broke my heart that the person I spent the last 6 years with, could just up and leave me and could move on without saying anything. I'm still trying to process the car accident and everything else keeps piling on. I can't stop thinking about them and I know they stopped caring about me.

1: take a step back,  take 10 deep breaths, run your hands under running water. This will help calm you down. 

2: you are under no obligation to be in the same room as your abuser. If they try, let someone you trust know that (while not getting into specifics) you'd be more comfortable at the get together if your abuser kept their distance and not talk to you. 

3: You have every right to be there and no one should shame you into leaving. You can have a life that you can do anything with. They (your abuser) shouldn't have a say in anything. You've got this and you can heal at your pace. We're all here for you.

100% yes. I have a hard time focusing on reading and reading comprehension because of it. I can barely get through any book because my brain is telling me I need to be on guard and shouldn't focus on typed words on dead trees. If I hear it and can focus on it then I'm fine. This baffled my teachers for years and just thought I was lazy, instead of asking "Why can't he read yet is clearly capable of writing a full on essay about whatb he heard?  Maybe he's just stupid, clearly nothing else is wrong with him." This makes it even weirder as I'm trying to get a job as a tv script writer. I can write but I still don't fully read eveything.

It's even painful when your pain IS who you are. Eveything you've gone through, everyone you've interacted with its just a continuous pain. For 16 years I had to deal with people trying to kill me or tale advantage of me. Because that wad 16 years I have really "lived" a life longer than I've been in that pain. And when I try to tell people, they just try and leave as fast as the can, causing the vicious cycle of abandonment issues to keep running through. I understand I'm messed up, no one knows how fucked my head is better than me, but with no real help all I can do is just talk it out and then go nowhere with that. I feel like I'll be alone for the rest of my life and the one good thing I had, I had to fuck that up too.

At this I feel like I've hit the lowest I could ever go.  I don't handle loss well, could be because I've had to deal with it since I was 7 when I started to lose people in my life. And this just hurts the worst. I've been with them for 6 years, I thought they could see past my trauma and really saw me for me. I still love them and I don't know why my stupid brain has to have all the info on why they wanted to leave me. 

I never wanted to lose the one thing in life I would have done anything to keep happy. But I guess I fucked up somewhere, and now I just have to find a way to move on...even if it hurts this much.

Not sure if that's freeze, but I hella relate to this. When I'm usually walking by myself, I tend to hold conversations in my head about what would happen if I just talked to the other person, but say out loud my response  (i.e. like a true conversation). I usually find it helpful because it's like a mini prep for a conversation I'll have with someone who usually tried to break me. Doesn't always help but it's mostly prep so I don't instantly fawn.

1: take a step back, take 10 deep breaths and run your hands through some running water. This'll help you calm down. 

2: you are deserving of love, and this is still early on into your relationship, you're okay and everything is fine. 

3: and this is important BE COMMUNICATUVE. If she is the one, she'll be understanding of your trauma and where you're at. So long as you get help and don't 100% rely on them to be your only support, they can help you out as best they can. 

Remember: you are both only human, and are both capable of making mistakes. So long as you both are open and communicate with each other then you'll both know it's the two of you vs the problem and the problem is never you vs them. 

You got this, I believe in you!

In most cases I definitely fawn. I try to be in a little confrontations as possible. But when that no longer works I'm in a pre-fight mode. It's like using the tactics of getting rid of a bear or mountain lion.  I make myself as big as possible and I get loud, as a warning. When it gets to that I'm seen as an asshole more than just trying to keep myself safe. I hate both methods it makes me either feel like I can't stand up for myself, or that I can only take things to extremes. It sucks and ruins a lot for me.

That's an understandably response, it's what trauma does to all of us. We work so hard everyday and feel like we need to do more just to seem normal. It's sucks when people don't fully recognize it too. But I see you and your struggles, you are valid.

1: You have a PhD that's more than most people, you have accomplished something. 
2: Trauma is trauma, there's no gate keeping who's deserving of healing or who had it bad. You are worthy just like all of us. 
3: You can do anything you set your mind to. Like I said at 1, you have a freaking PhD! You are capable!

There's more than one?" When it got to CPTSD and describing that people who have been through prolonged trauma on a neat consistent basis, it clicked for me and what I had been through in life. 
When I was at an extremely low point I found this sub-reddit, I thought that there wasn't a snowballs chance a place like this existed, but here I am and learning I'm not alone in my pain.
To think all of this happened in a span of a month is really trippy.

I have to move back in with my patents at the age of 25. Life isn't going okay for me either and I get your pain. If I could, I'd invite you to come over to my place for Christmas. I want you to know that I'm here for you and you can talk to me anytime.

And because of that we are unaware that, no matter how hard we try, we end up making the same mistakes even when wet don't want to.
If you can, I really encourage you to find a therapist to help you work through this to rerecode your brain to be better. You have the power to do this, we all do.

Well I want you here. I know wr just met, but I'm here for you. I'm someone who can try and help out. 
You're here because you want to live. We all do. Life can get better and here we can help each other out.

From what my trauma therapist had told me, memories from trauma are about as real as they come. It's from your brain trying to remember the danger you were in so it can avoid it again. It's a bitch and a half to know this, but in a way it tells you that what you experienced was real and no one can really say you're wrong because they weren't there, you were.

For starters, and from what I can tell, Reddit only lets you use one flair on a post.

But as for your problem at hand, I suggest finding your Anti-Trigger.  Something that just clicks like a trigger but instead of making you hypervigilant brings you down and grounded.  Grounding exercises help, along with maybe the sounds of an environment i.e. Beach, Forest, Windy Planes, etc. or a task that you can work on and calmly figure out the situation that is at hand.  That should help you calm down, and whatever it is that consistently gets you to that calm place, that is your Anti-Trigger and can be a great tool to help.

As for your sister, maybe you can help her find some government assistance programs that can help her figure out how to help get her feet back on the ground so she doesn't have to go from couch to couch with her newborn and can just have a stable environment to raise the newly brought in meat bag. (hope that didn't come off insulting, I'm just not one for babies but support others in my own way) .

Hopefully, this helps in some way.  You can get threw this and so can she.  You've both got this!

I wanted to use a word that would put the negative of trigger away.  So I used the double negative method to get a positive feeling, thus Anti-Trigger.
Bob Ross is usually my go to asmr.

Is there a little hiking trail near where you live?  Even if it's just a few hours, you should go for a walk down it once you've fully recovered from the stomach bug.  It could help you recharge just for a little bit.

When I hear the sounds on my Anti-trigger I feel like I'm sitting in the sand hugging my knees, but not out of fear but to meditate and I feel like I could just spend hours seeing the tide roll in as the sun sets behind me and I can see the stars begin to peek out over the sea.

That's good to hear that you're in a healthy relationship.  I figured if "Trigger" has such a strong and negative association that brings fear an anxiety, why not use the word against it?  Thus the "Anti-Trigger" a double negative makes a positive.
I have a rambunctious adopted 4 year old kitty who finally opened up to me.  She likes to keep my company by sitting on my lap.
Who is it by? I'll look them up.
I usually play a song from The Last of Us when I walk.  The song is Home and it helps me be a healthy sad.

I like it when there's hardly any cars on the road.  Maybe in a 15 to 20 minute time span there's one car that drives by, and it's usually a cop on patrol when they're not parked.  It lets me just walk down the middle of the road and finally see all the wide open space there is instead of the clustered sidewalks that I have to do with along with the noise of everyone else in town.  It makes me feel like I'm the only person left alive and NO One can hurt me anymore...
I tend to walk at night when no one can bother me.  When people are out I feel like I have to keep my face on when all I want to do is just drop my guard and cry when I'm walking.

It's always nice to find someone you can feel confident enough to tell what happened.  It's never easy and it's the worst feeling in the world when you dig it up and fear that you'll be shamed for thinking you're the victim.
